summary: Compare a finite set of supplied CityGML-derived urban alternatives by stable feature identity, CRS, epoch and declared attribute/geometry changes, without inferring semantics from meshes or running an urban simulation.
objective: Compare a finite set of supplied CityGML-derived urban alternatives by stable feature identity, CRS, epoch and declared attribute/geometry changes, without inferring semantics from meshes or running an urban simulation.
example_prompts: Build citygml stable-id scenario differencer with explicit stable IDs, units, time, boundary inputs and stale/unavailable states.
not_for: Safety certification, regulatory compliance, or operational control without qualified local review.

entities.name: Base registry
entities.guidance: Retain dataset/version hash, CRS with axis order/units, epoch and stable featureID/identifier separately from glTF node names.

entities.name: Scenario patches
entities.guidance: Each finite alternative lists add/remove/replace operations against base IDs with provenance and expected prior hash.

entities.name: Difference view
entities.guidance: Report semantic attribute changes and geometry-hash changes independently; missing mapping stays unavailable.

state_contract.model: Accept one base registry and 2..16 finite supplied scenario patch sets. Require unique featureID, declared CRS/axis order/linear units and common epoch or an explicit prevalidated transform. Apply transactionally: add requires an absent target ID and null predecessor hash; update/remove requires an existing target and exact expected prior hash. Reject duplicate operations on one ID unless a declared sequential patch order and intermediate hashes are present. Compare every scenario with the same immutable base hash; report added, removed, semantic-changed, geometry-changed and mapping-unavailable IDs. Never recover CityGML class, topology or identifier from visual mesh similarity.
state_contract.authority: The CityGML-derived registry, CRS/epoch, base hash and scenario patches own identity/change state. Blender may author context geometry but must preserve an external ID map; glTF transports render meshes/nodes; Three.js applies patches to cloned registries and drives selection/difference overlays.

invariants: Every add targets an absent ID with null predecessor; every update/remove matches an existing ID and exact prior hash.
Alternatives share the same base registry hash.
Semantic and geometry changes remain separate.
Unmapped meshes never acquire inferred CityGML semantics.
motion_guidance: Playback restores stored model/event steps; animation between steps is explanatory and never changes authoritative counts, timestamps or completion state.
creative_affordances: Use cutaways, small multiples, queues and non-color status glyphs while keeping assumptions and unavailable states visible.
known_limits: No planning merit, environmental effect, BIM correctness, topology recovery or regulatory conclusion is computed.

claims.statement: OGC CityGML 3.0 defines a semantic information model alongside geometry and relationships; geographic features have mandatory featureID for versions and an optional identifier that can reference the same real-world object across versions.
claims.scope: CityGML 3.0 Conceptual Model and Users Guide; this recipe’s patch hashes and comparison categories are authored workflow rules.

source_refs.locator: Sections 7 and 7.2.1, semantic modeling and feature identity

object_craft.structure: Blender exports named context/building/road meshes and an external featureID-to-node manifest in the declared display frame; glTF mesh structure is not treated as semantic source.
object_craft.material: Added/removed/attribute/geometry changes use distinct hatch/glyph channels.
object_craft.articulation: Three.js validates the ID manifest, clones the base, applies one patch transaction and synchronizes camera/selection across alternatives.

physical_contract.scope: Transactional comparison of supplied semantic/geometry records; no urban physics.
